testimonials.quote: I came to the fellowship with a lot of questions. What I found was a room full of students who took the Bible seriously and welcomed me anyway. I have grown more in one year here than I expected.
testimonials.name: A student at UR-CST

testimonials.quote: The Thursday study gave my week a centre. I used to drift through campus life. Now I have a place to open the Word, pray, and be honest with people who point me back to Christ.

testimonials.quote: Before I joined, I thought following Jesus was mostly about being good. The teaching here helped me see the gospel clearly — and gave me a community to grow in.
testimonials.name: A student at ETO Nyamata

testimonials.quote: I started watching online because I could not get to a fellowship. The conversations were honest, and they eventually connected me to a group where I could grow in person.

articles.title: Three ways we make disciples
articles.excerpt: Our mission is simple, but it takes shape in ordinary, weekly faithfulness. Here is how we pursue it.
articles.imageAlt: Students working together during a ministry training session

paragraphs: Christian Students Network exists to make disciples of Jesus Christ and strengthen believers in the gospel. That mission is not carried by one event or one program. It is carried by a rhythm of teaching, training, and reaching — three ministry expressions that shape our life together.

sections.heading: 1. Weekly discipleship classes
paragraphs: We equip students in high schools and universities across Rwanda by establishing weekly discipleship groups that foster spiritual growth, deeper biblical understanding, and Christ-centred living. These groups are where the Bible is opened, questions are asked, and students learn to follow Jesus in the ordinary places of campus life.

sections.heading: 2. Strengthen Conferences
paragraphs: We organise national, regional, and targeted conferences to present the gospel clearly, train students, and call them to deeper commitment to Christ. Conferences give us a wider room to teach, to worship together, and to send students back to their campuses with fresh conviction.

sections.heading: 3. Digital resources
paragraphs: We expand gospel reach through weekly online sessions, long-form teaching on YouTube, short video content, and the translation and distribution of gospel materials in Kinyarwanda. For students who are far away, or who are exploring the faith for the first time, these resources make the Word accessible.

sections.heading: Faithfulness over novelty
paragraphs: None of these expressions is complicated. They are simply ways of being faithful with the gospel: teach the Word, train believers, and reach the next student. We pray that this rhythm continues to produce disciples who love Christ, love His church, and proclaim His supremacy to the ends of the earth.

articles.title: The Bible: our supreme and final authority
articles.excerpt: Everything we do as a fellowship is measured by the Scriptures. Here is what we believe about the Word of God.
articles.imageAlt: Open Bibles on a table during a Bible study

paragraphs: As a network of students, we want to be shaped by the Scriptures rather than by the mood of the moment. Our statement of faith begins with the Bible because everything else we believe flows from it.

sections.heading: Fully inspired, without error
paragraphs: We believe that the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, consisting of all 66 books, are the fully inspired, inerrant, infallible, and sufficient Word of God. In their original writings, they are without error and reveal God's complete truth for faith, life, and godliness.

sections.heading: Our final authority
paragraphs: The Bible stands as the supreme and final authority on all matters of truth, morality, and the proper conduct of mankind. That means we do not sit in judgment over the text. We come to it ready to be taught, corrected, and shaped.

sections.heading: A Word to live by
paragraphs: Because the Scriptures are sufficient, we do not need to look elsewhere for a word about how to live as followers of Jesus. In our classes and conferences, in our online teaching, and in our friendships, the aim is the same: to know what God has said and to obey it.

scripture.text: All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness.

articles.title: Why we gather on Thursday
articles.excerpt: Every Thursday in Kicukiro, students open the Scriptures together. Here is what happens — and why you are invited.
articles.imageAlt: Students worshipping together in a conference hall

paragraphs: Thursday is not a random day on our calendar. It is the day we set aside to gather, open the Word, and encourage one another in the middle of a busy week. Students come from different campuses, different backgrounds, and different places in their walk with Christ — and we study together.

sections.heading: A midweek anchor
paragraphs: University and high school life moves quickly. Assignments, exams, work, and family responsibilities can crowd out the things that matter most. A weekly gathering gives us a fixed point: a time to be reminded of the gospel, to pray, and to sit under the Bible with other believers.

sections.heading: Three sessions, one aim
paragraphs: We meet at Kicukiro – Mu Banyamakuru with three sessions across the day: 11:00 AM – 1:00 PM, 2:00 PM – 3:30 PM, and 4:00 PM – 5:00 PM. The sessions make room for different schedules, but the aim is the same: that every student who comes would leave with a clearer sight of Christ.

sections.heading: Come as you are
paragraphs: You do not need to have it all together to join us. Bring your Bible, bring your questions, and bring a friend. If you are not sure where to start, call +250 784 857 707 and we will help you find the right session.

scripture.text: And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together.

statementOfFaith.title: The Bible
paragraphs: We believe that the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, consisting of all 66 books, are the fully inspired, inerrant, infallible, and sufficient Word of God. In their original writings, they are without error and reveal God's complete truth for faith, life, and godliness. The Bible stands as the supreme and final authority on all matters of truth, morality, and the proper conduct of mankind.

statementOfFaith.title: God
paragraphs: We believe in the one true God — the Creator of heaven and earth — who eternally exists in three persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. He created and upholds all things by the Word of His power, and in Him we live and move and have our being.
The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit share the same divine nature, attributes, and perfection, and are worthy of the same worship, trust, and obedience. All things exist for His glory.
statementOfFaith.scripture: Genesis 1:1, 26–27; Deuteronomy 32:4; Psalm 9:8; Matthew 28:19–20; John 1:1–4, 17:3; Acts 17:28; 2 Corinthians 13:4; Hebrews 1:3; Revelation 4:11

statementOfFaith.title: The Holy Spirit
paragraphs: We believe in the Holy Spirit, the third Person of the Triune God, who is fully divine and active in all the works of God. He inspired the Scriptures, convicts the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment, and regenerates all who believe in Jesus Christ.

At the moment of salvation, He baptizes every believer into the body of Christ, indwells, seals, and empowers them for godly living, service, and witness. The Holy Spirit glorifies Christ, cultivates Christian character, bestows spiritual gifts for the building up of the Church, and unites believers in love and purpose. His abiding presence is the believer's guarantee of final redemption and transformation into the likeness of Christ.

statementOfFaith.title: Man in His Fallen State
paragraphs: We believe that humanity was uniquely created in the image of God to reflect His glory. However, through voluntary rebellion against God, mankind fell from a state of innocence and became sinful by nature and by choice.
As a result, all people are separated from God, under just condemnation, and incapable of living for His glory apart from salvation in Jesus Christ.

statementOfFaith.title: Christ
paragraphs: We believe in Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the second person of the Trinity, who is fully God and fully man. He was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the virgin Mary, and lived a sinless life.

He died on the cross as a substitutionary sacrifice for the sins of humanity, and all who believe in Him are justified by His shed blood. Jesus rose bodily from the dead, ascended to heaven, and now serves as our High Priest and Advocate at the right hand of the Father. He will one day return in glory to judge the living and the dead.
statementOfFaith.scripture: Isaiah 9:6; Matthew 1:22–23; John 1:1–5, 14:10–30; Acts 1:9–11; Romans 1:3–4; 1 Corinthians 15:3–4; 1 Timothy 3:16; 6:14–15; Titus 2:13; Hebrews 4:14–15

statementOfFaith.title: Salvation & Security of Salvation
paragraphs: We teach that the Lord Jesus Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, as a representative and substitutionary sacrifice. All who by faith receive Him as their personal Savior are justified by His shed blood, born again of the Holy Spirit, and thereby made eternally secure as children of God.

At the moment of salvation, the Holy Spirit baptizes the believer into the body of Christ. Salvation is a free gift of God's grace, received solely through faith in the person and finished work of Jesus Christ, apart from human effort or merit. Because it is God's gift, salvation is eternal and cannot be lost.
statementOfFaith.scripture: John 1:12; 14:6; Romans 5:1; 6:23; Galatians 3:26; Ephesians 2:8–9; Titus 3:5; John 10:29; Romans 8:37–39; 2 Corinthians 5:21; 1 Corinthians 12:13; 2 Timothy 1:12; Hebrews 7:25; 10:10, 14; 1 Peter 1:3–5

statementOfFaith.title: Resurrection & Eternity
paragraphs: We believe in the bodily resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, His ascension into heaven, and His present ministry as our High Priest and Advocate. We also believe in the bodily resurrection of both the just and the unjust — resulting in eternal life for the redeemed in the presence of God, and eternal separation from God in hell for those who reject salvation in Christ.
Heaven and hell are real, eternal realities: eternal union with God for the saved, and eternal punishment apart from Him for the lost.
statementOfFaith.scripture: Matthew 25:46; John 3:16; 5:28–29; Romans 6:23; Acts 1:3, 9; Hebrews 7:25–26; Revelation 20:15

statementOfFaith.title: The Church
paragraphs: We believe that the Church is the universal Body of Christ and the one family of God, made up of all who have been redeemed by Jesus Christ and regenerated by the Holy Spirit. Upon accepting Christ as Savior and Lord, all believers become members of His body, the Church.

The local church is a visible expression of this universal Church, composed of baptized believers who gather regularly for worship, prayer, teaching of the Word, fellowship, observance of the ordinances (baptism and the Lord's Supper), and service. Through the power of the Holy Spirit, the Church exists to grow in spiritual maturity, to walk in love and unity, and to fulfill the Great Commission for the glory of Christ.
